==Biography==
Before his professional League of Legends career, Kevin "'''kev1n'''" Rubiszewski played Counter Strike: Source, at a competitive level. He was introduced to League of Legends by other members of his clan, and despite having no prior knowledge of the MOBA genre, went on to climb the solo queue ladder just months later.

===Season 1===
Due to his impressive play in solo queue, in February 2011, kev1n was offered a place as top laner at newly formed [[Team gamed!de]] along with [[CandyPanda]] and [[Nyph]]. His first major tournament came in the form of the [[Riot Season 1 Championship|Season 1 World Championship]]. The team ended up placing 6th after losing to [[Counter Logic Gaming]] in the 5th place match.
 
===Pre-Season 2===
Just 5 days after the end of the tournament, the roster of [[Team gamed!de]] disbanded, leaving kev1n team-less. This was until he was picked up by [[against All authority]], who he had previously been beaten by at the [[Riot Season 1 Championship|World Championships]]. Kev1n was part of an entirely new roster, as aAa's old lineup left for [[Millenium]]. His time here was short-lived, with the roster disbanding soon after.

===Season 2===
After [[Wickd]]'s departure, kev1n was signed by [[SK Gaming]], and here played again with both [[CandyPanda]] and [[Nyph]], along with [[ocelote]]. His first chance to impress with his new team came at [[IEM Season VI - Global Challenge Kiev|IEM Kiev]], where he competed against the likes of [[Moscow 5]] and [[TSM]]. SK ended up coming in 4th overall after being beaten by Moscow 5 in the semi-finals.  

Later on in the year came a period of role changes for kev1n. He initially switched roles with ocelote, making him the midlaner of the team. This change didn't last long, and soon saw the pair switch back to their original roles. Soon after, upon [[CandyPanda]]'s departure, [[YoungBuck]] joined SK, pushing kev1n into the AD carry position. Again the switch was ineffective, resulting in YoungBuck leaving 2 weeks later and kev1n moving back to the top lane.

With kev1n back in his natural role, SK placed 3rd at [[European Challenger Circuit: Poland|ECC Poland]] with [[Araneae]] and [[YellOwStaR]] now on the team. Hitting a run of good form, SK now faced the challenge of performing at the [[Season 2/Regional Finals - Cologne|Season 2 Regional Finals]]. The tournament was a success, with the team placing 2nd and qualifying for the [[Season 2 World Championship]].

Unfortunately, the World Championship was not a success for kev1n and SK, with the team losing all 3 games.

===Season 3===
Despite qualifying for the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/Season 3/Spring Round Robin|Spring Split]] of the LCS, SK Gaming had a relatively poor start to Season 3, as the [[IEM Season VII - World Championship|IEM World Championship]] saw kev1n and SK go out in the group stages along with [[Evil Geniuses.EU|Evil Geniuses]] and [[Fnatic]].

Fortunately, after a shaky start, the team picked up its pace over the course of spring split, with the assistance of kev1n's impressive performances in the top lane on more than one occasion. SK finished 3rd, guaranteeing them a place in the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/Season 3/Spring Playoffs|Spring Playoffs]]. The playoffs were not a success, with SK finising 4th, without winning a single game, [[Gambit Gaming|Gambit]] beating them 2-0 in the semifinals.

The exceedingly tight [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/Season 3/Summer Round Robin|Summer Split]] was far less successful than the spring split. Despite only having 2 less wins than 2nd place [[Fnatic]], SK came in 7th after losing to [[Team Alternate]] in a 6th place tiebreaker.

This marked at the end of kev1n's time at SK, as he left to join [[Ninjas in Pyjamas]], but this did not last long; he left only two months later to join [[Team Alternate]].

===2014 Season===
Along with his teammates, kev1n chose to leave the organization and join [[Millenium]], retaining their spot for the upcoming [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/2014 Season/Spring Round Robin|Spring Split]].

Soon after came kev1n's first major tournament win at [[IEM Season VIII - Sao Paulo|IEM Sao Paulo]], with Millenium not dropping a single game over the course of the tournament.

Millenium's first split with the their new roster was tough, seeing kev1n and his teammates finish last overall, despite his generally positive performances on a range of champions. This resulted in Millenium's participation in the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/2014 Season/Summer Promotion|Summer Promotion]]. Millenium beat Ninjas in Pyjamas 3-2 to secure their place in the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/2014 Season/Summer Round Robin|Summer Split]], with kev1n being the clear MVP over the series.

Millenium started the Summer Split particularly well, ending week one in 2nd place behind [[Alliance]]. The split was an improvement on spring, finishing 5th overall. kev1n continued to impress, consistently being one of the standout players on the team, along with midlaner [[Kerp]]. With this, Millenium qualified for the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/2014 Season/Summer Playoffs|Summer Playoffs]]. For kev1n in particular, the playoffs were a huge disappointment, and Millenium came in 6th, not winning a single game. 

===2015 Season===
[[Millenium]]'s playoff woes meant that they had to fight for their LCS status in the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/2015 Season/Spring Promotion|Spring Promotion]]. A close fought match-up with [[Unicorns of Love]] ultimately saw kev1n and Millenium lose 2-3.

kev1n participated with [[Millenium]] in the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/2015 Season/Spring Expansion|Expansion Tournament]]. The team received a bye for Round 1, but were eliminated from the tournament in Round 2 after being beaten by [[GIANTS! Gaming]].

Ahead of Week 5 of the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/2015 Season/Spring Season|Spring Split]], kev1n joined [[Elements]], replacing [[Wickd]].<ref>[http://twitter.com/Kev1nTV/status/567774051444473858/photo/1 kev1n's Tweet] ''twitter.com''</ref> He played with the team for 2 weeks, and remained with [[Elements]] as a substitute after [[Wickd]]'s return to the starting roster. 

== Trivia ==
* Is of Polish descent, born in Berlin.
* During May 2012, Kev1n switched lanes with [[Ocelote]], the AP mid. Later, Ocelote switched back to AP, while Kev1n switched to AD.
* After [[Candy Panda]] left SK in June of 2012, Kevin became their new AD carry.
* In [[xPeke]]'s famous Kassadin backdoor attempt at [[IEM Season VII - Global Challenge Katowice|IEM Katowice 2013]] he tried to defend the Nexus on [[Olaf]] without a Flash. He missed 2 crucial axes which lead to xPeke surviving with 39hp and winning the game.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XdN67NuhMW4 xPeke backdoor vs. SK Gaming (Intel Extreme Masters Katowice)] ''youtube.com''</ref>
* His favorite champion is {{ci|Irelia}}.<ref>[http://www.team-dignitas.net/articles/blogs/League-of-Legends/1963/Interview-with-SK-Kev1n-I-changed-from-top-to-AD-because-of-one-reason-and-that-is-Darien-from-M5/ Interview with SK Kev1n: "I changed from top to AD because of one reason and that is Darien from M5"] ''team-dignitas.net''</ref>
* First game played was Red Alert 2, which he got from his uncle.
* Name was inspired by professional Counter Strike player Edward.
